item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The numerous "what-ifs" jammed together for this really don't cohere, and at least in some cases are so incompatible with one another that I doubt they ever could.
"Creepypasta spooks wish they could be SCPs" is, while much too cute for me on its face, maybe not completely dead out of the gate. But combining it with "what if Foundation leadership held auditions for prospective SCPs," as well as "what if top Foundation personnel had extranarrative awareness and were concerned with 'marketability' in allocating containment resources"—two premises goofy enough that they would need particularly interesting elaboration/complication and careful handling to ever work individually, let alone in combination—lands this solidly in "lol random" territory.
Easy downvote.

item.content:encoded:
+1, not for being funny, but for serving as a genuinely good guide for newbies. Lots of them start with Eldritch-esqe creatures like this, then wonder why they keep flunking after every single post. The answer: it's not about "who's the most overpowered," but "who has the best stories." There's no substitute for good writing, and everyone needs to know that.

That said, it's still funny in its own rights.

item.content:encoded: Trevor Henderson has stated that he does not want Siren Head on the SCP wiki. Community members should please respect that decision.

item.title: Re: In light of recent events...
item.content:encoded:
Considering that Siren Head isn't licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0, and that this wiki's license prohibits the distribution of such a character which isn't non-compliant, that tale probably won't be coming into existence licensing-wise.

From a community standpoint, there have been attempts to eulogize about this (admittedly minor, in the grand scheme of things) situation in the form of an SCP document/other article format, most of which have failed to stay on the site for very long. As such, I doubt that the tale probably wouldn't survive very long, especially when coupled with the possibility of being somewhat derivative of the idea put forward in this tale.

item.content:encoded: Turns out that "Zalgo" is just his stage name. His real name is "Zelbert Aloysious Legolas Gertrude O'Malley" and he got teased a lot as a wee abomination-let. Joining the SCP Foundation would have been validation that he was finally a cool kid instead of the dork that got picked on in high school. Believe me, swirlies are even less pleasant when you have a dozen heads getting swirlied at the same time. And do you have any idea how hard it is to find an orthodontist who can install non-Euclidean braces?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Zalgo wasn't even supposed to be actually scary when it was first thought up. It was initially a parody of all those Lovecraftian abomination monster thingies and the over-the-top pseudo-Lovecraft style purple prose used to describe them, as well as of those lighthearted comics, cartoons and whatnot it was edited into.

But then some younger internet surfers who didn't know any better tried to pass Zalgo off as some serious horror monster, and things sorta declined from there.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's true that we only keep articles that are interesting, even though the Foundation, if it existed, would contain any anomalous item. However, this isn't real life. This is fiction. Each article is a narrative of sorts, and has to succeed as such. It has to be interesting enough to be worth reading. Much of real life is boring and repetitive. That doesn't excuse stories that are boring and repetitive, even if they're nominally based on real life.
